thread:
Oncall Bot: SEV2 alert - elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in hosted-us-east · paging alex, lucas. Start time: 2026-03-10T14:02:58Z. Link: https://incidents.redwood/example/1830245678 :rotating_light:
Alex: I’m on it. Joining bridge now. Scaling up inference pool and checking recent deploys.
Lucas: I’m looking at traces — saw a spike in model kernel errors around 14:00, many clients timed out during kv-cache write. Possible regression from the last runtime kernel swap.
Alex: On bridge (zoom.us/j/xxxxx). Rolling traffic to previous kernel variant (route: model-x -> model-x-v1). Will update routing policy to prefer warm KV cache nodes.
SRE Lead: Handoff note — plan temporary routing + increase pool by 2x for the next 30m, then revert if stable. Keep customer-visible comms minimal until we know impact. Please capture timeline for RCA.
Alex: Mitigation applied: routing changed at 14:08Z, scaling +2 nodes at 14:09Z. Error rate dropped ~70% within 3 minutes. Still seeing ~5% elevated errors for long-tail requests.
Jane (Support): Which customer accounts hit this? We have 4 paying accounts with sustained errors >5min. Need a statuspage block + short note for affected customers.
Lucas: Affected buckets: org-113, org-504, org-298, org-711. Root cause appears to be an interaction between a new quantized kernel and a subset of long-context workloads that cause KV cache writes to throw OOM in the runtime path.
Tom (Product): Can we set a timeline for a postmortem and a public RCA? Recommend internal postmortem within 48h and a customer-facing RCA within 5 business days. Who owns the internal doc?
Amy (Customer Success): I’ll lead outbound comms. Need a statuspage draft now and an RCA timeline we can share with top accounts. Also propose offering credits to the 4 affected customers as a goodwill gesture — need approval flow.
Alex: Internal postmortem meeting proposal: 2026-03-11 09:30 PT (48h) — attendees: SRE, Eng Runtime, Product, Support, CS. Owner: Alex. Customer-facing RCA publish target: 2026-03-17. Owner: Tom + Amy.
SRE Lead: Action items I’m logging now (please add ticket IDs):
- ENG-RT-2154: Revert risky kernel selection for quantized path (owner: Lucas, due: 2026-03-12)
- SRE-2667: Add e2e test to simulate long-context kv-cache behavior (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-19)
- MON-3111: Tune alert thresholds to surface noisy kv-cache errors earlier (owner: oncall, due: 2026-03-13)
Lucas: Creating ENG-RT-2154 now. Quick debug commands to collect repro logs:```shell
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference --since=30m | grep "kv_cache" -A4 -B4 > /tmp/kv-dump.log
gzip /tmp/kv-dump.log && gcs-cli cp /tmp/kv-dump.log.gz gs://redwood-debug/1830245678-dump.gz
```Link to debug dump: https://storage.redwood/1830245678-dump.gz
Jane (Support): Statuspage draft (short block) - please review:```
Incident: Elevated errors for text generation in hosted-us-east
Impact: Some customers experienced increased failures for requests to /v1/generate between 14:00–14:12 UTC.
Action: We rolled back a runtime kernel variant and increased capacity; errors reduced significantly.
Next update: We will provide a detailed RCA within five business days.
```Suggest adding contact line for affected customers.
Amy (Customer Success): Text tweak: change "rolled back a runtime kernel variant" -> "we reverted a recent runtime change that affected a subset of long-context workloads". Also add: "Customers impacted directly will receive an email with next steps and any credits." I’ll prepare the customer email template.
Alex: ACK. Added note and contact line. Statuspage publish time if no objections: 14:30Z. Tom please sign off on timeline for public RCA.
Tom (Product): Timeline OK. Request that the public RCA include: timeline, technical root cause, mitigation, and long-term remediation plan + ETA. Also include the list of affected org IDs (consent checked).
Alex: Confirming bridge handoff to SRE Lead at 14:25Z. Oncall handoff done. I’ll track the postmortem doc and populate the initial timeline + logs link.
SRE Lead: I’ll run the postmortem and schedule follow-ups. High-level remediation plan: 1) Preventive: add kernel-selection guardrails, 2) Detection: expand unit + e2e tests and provide synthetic traffic to long-context paths, 3) Recovery: automated fallback to prior kernel on specific kv-cache error signatures.
Lucas: Quick note about diagnostics — please preserve affected container images and set image tags to avoid GC. Command:```shell
kubectl annotate pod <pod-name> redwood/incident-1830245678=preserve
```
Jane (Support): I’ll draft the customer email now and share for approval. Amy will lead the call invites for top accounts.
Amy (Customer Success): I’ve started an outreach list and will send a priority email after we publish the statuspage entry. I can run 1:1 calls for org-113 and org-504 if needed.
Alex: Final items: - Postmortem doc link: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/1830245678 (I’ll seed it after bridge notes) - Action owners assigned in the doc - Follow-up meeting in one week to verify remediation progress. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
SRE Lead: Thanks Alex. I’ll open the follow-up tickets and add them to the weekly engineering sync. Marking this thread as the canonical incident thread for tracking.
Jane (Support): Published statuspage at 14:31Z. Link: https://status.redwood/incident/1830245678
Amy (Customer Success): Sending first outreach email at 14:35Z to affected contacts; I’ll CC Tom and Jane.
Alex: Closing operational bridge. If anyone sees regressions, re-open paging. Good job team.
